table1.title: Table 1 Selected evidence and limits of inference
rows:
L-R01
2016 Medicare survey
Patient sex association
Female versus male adjusted odds of any cost-related nonadherence: under 65, 1.66 (95% CI 1.31–2.10); 65 or older, 1.21 (1.04–1.41).
Cross-sectional self-report; residual confounding and eligibility uncertainty. Not a current policy effect or causal bias estimate.

L-R02
Selected Chicago cohort
Patient sex association
Adjusted persistent nonadherence OR 1.36 (0.95–1.95); transient nonadherence OR 0.81 (0.62–1.07), women versus men.
Both intervals include the null. Selected population; longitudinal outcomes differ from annual occurrence.

L-P01 and L-P02
Selected procedure pairs
L-P01: 55 pairs; male-associated work RVUs averaged 30% higher. L-P02: no significant aggregate work-RVU or RVU-per-minute difference.
Different matches and estimands. L-P02 abstract/companion pair counts conflict. Null is not equivalence; valuation is not patient access.

L-P03
Time-based procedure model
Female versus male procedure labels: median work RVUs/hour 10.6 versus 9.7; modeled specialty compensation $555 versus $599/hour.
Compensation multipliers are not Medicare conversion factors. Procedure/payer comparability and full-episode work remain concerns.

L-G05
Male fracture outreach
7,842 analyzed
BMD testing 10.7% versus 4.9%; adjusted OR 2.13 (1.74–2.62). Treatment initiation 4.0% versus 2.5%; adjusted OR 1.59 (1.19–2.12).
28.3% excluded after randomization. Bundled outreach; no fracture reduction, isolated software effect or sex-gap closure established.

L-T01
MA COPD invitation trial
19,113 randomized
Intention-to-treat proportion of days covered: +3.8 percentage points (3.1–4.5). Exacerbation and total-spending estimates did not establish benefit.
Refills are not inhaler use or clinical control. Low-income subsidy beneficiaries excluded. Intervention bundled cost sharing and management.

L-T02
MA benefit-tool implementation
Difference-in-differences patient prescription spending: +1.2% (−0.7 to 3.0). Total prescription spending and monthly fills also compatible with no change.
Nonrandom implementation; no demonstrated average improvement. No intervention-by-sex effect or equity benefit established.

L-T03
Post hoc cluster-trial report
Medicare orders
Overall fill difference +0.5 percentage points (−2.4 to 3.4). Highest-cost drug-class subgroup +10.5 points (1.9–19.2).
Subgroup exploratory; its Medicare denominator unreported. L-T03-P1 is the same trial. Selected eligible orders; no equity-gap closure.
table1.note: Examples from selected retrieval, not a complete included-study table or pooled analysis. Confidence intervals are 95%. MA, Medicare Advantage; OR, odds ratio; BMD, bone mineral density; RVU, relative value unit. Patient identity eligibility and formal independent appraisal remain unresolved. All numeric findings are provisional extractions with source locations retained in the working register and intervention evidence file.

table2.title: Table 2 Unranked opportunities and the next useful study
headers: Patient benefit or research contribution to test
rows:
O-01
Medication affordability
Resolve clinically appropriate prescriptions through benefit information plus pharmacist or clinician support; measure unmet medication need and disease-specific outcomes.
Pragmatic trial against existing tools and navigation. Bundled program benefit coexists with null average benefit-tool results. [L-T01; L-T02; L-T03]

O-02
Post-fracture follow-up
Complete appropriate bone assessment and treatment after a qualifying fracture, with accessible human follow-up.
Multisite trial; separate process improvement from later fracture outcomes. Existing male-only outreach has substantial post-assignment exclusions. [L-G05]

O-03
Non-drug authorization
Reduce avoidable delay and patient burden for clinically indicated services; preserve clinical review and alternatives.
Controlled rollout with all clinically eligible patients in the denominator. Final API rules enable workflows; they do not establish a sex disparity or product benefit. [P-046; P-047]

O-04
Procedure valuation research
Improve resource measurement, clinically defensible matching and reproducibility of code comparisons.
Independent full-episode work measurement and replication before policy-effect claims. Opposing findings require explanation. [L-P01; L-P02; L-P03]

O-05
Lymphedema fulfillment
Improve timely fitting, delivery and usable compression treatment; measure function and patient burden.
Post-2024 needs audit, then controlled fulfillment intervention. Historical costs precede the current Medicare benefit. [L-A01; L-A02; P-054]

O-06
Kidney education and support
Improve understanding, practical support and informed treatment choices at relevant kidney-disease stages.
US Medicare patient/caregiver needs assessment, followed by a controlled pilot. Existing clinician interviews are contextual, not measured Medicare outcomes. [L-Q01; P-055]
table2.note: Domains are organized by clinical and implementation problem, not ranked by profitability, market size or expected health gain. Direct Medicare payment for the proposed software, purchasing demand, incremental cost-effectiveness and equitable reach are unverified. Detailed data requirements, prospective users/buyers and study designs are provided in Supplement B and the opportunity workbook.
